newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - RWE 96/97 energy sales down, pft up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - RWE 96/97 energy sales down, pft up.

text.p: RWE Energie AG, the energy arm of diversified utility giant RWE AG, said on Wednesday its profits advanced some 10 percent in the year ended June 30 despite a slight slip in sales.
The company posted a one percent drop in sales to 16.25 billion marks ($9.3 billion), according to preliminary data.

But Chairman Roland Farnung told reporters that profits rose as a result of reduced costs and new income streams after RWE Energie took direct control of 16 shareholdings formerly controlled by RWE itself.
RWE Energie, Germany's largest electricity provider, reported a net profit of 485 million marks ($278 million) for the 1995/1996 business year.

Farnung said RWE had reconciled itself to the prospect of pressure on energy returns, with fierce competition likely to keep German household energy prices flat for some time, and said the group would react by upping efforts to cut costs.

Around 5,000 jobs had been cut at RWE Energie since 1993 through early retirement schemes. Further efforts to reduce personnel costs through more flexible working hours and overtime cuts were in progress.

Farnung said the company was also benefiting from cheaper energy supplies due to the re-opening of its Biblis A nuclear power station, after an unsuccessful attempt by the state of Hesse to close it down.
Farnung said RWE Energie aimed to further expand its foreign business.
"RWE Energie wants to be the leading private energy supplier in Europe," he said.
In addition, he said RWE was interested in buying into the state-owned German gas distribution firm Gasag. The city of Berlin is inviting bids for its 51 percent stake in the company.
